title: PLS-DA nominates exploratory serum-metabolite patterns in osteopenia
summary: Supervised PLS-DA and model-derived VIP feature scores helped nominate serum-metabolite patterns across bone-density groups in 220 adults. The study reported 30, 55 and 49 exploratory candidates for osteopenia versus controls, osteoporosis versus controls and osteoporosis versus osteopenia, using seven-fold cross-validation and permutation checks. All selected metabolites had FDR-adjusted q values above 0.05 and were retained under exploratory VIP, nominal-P and fold-change thresholds. The 135-person discovery and 85-person temporal replication groups came from one hospital; these findings do not establish prospective fracture prediction, external transport or clinical benefit.
organization: Wuhan Fourth Hospital; Wuchang University of Technology; Wuhan University; Fudan University

evidence.tested: PLS-DA group discrimination with seven-fold cross-validation and 200-permutation testing; VIP scores helped select exploratory serum-metabolite candidates across BMD groups.
evidence.unknown: All candidates had FDR-adjusted q>0.05; temporal replication was within the same hospital and study; no prospective fracture prediction, clinical benefit, or external transport was tested.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised PLS-DA learned separation between BMD groups; model-derived VIP scores contributed to candidate metabolite selection.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher PDF: abstract, cohort Methods, supervised PLS-DA training/VIP selection, cross-validation/permutation description, candidate q-value caveat and same-hospital temporal split.
